tone.voice: a great coach who pushes you but believes in you — no fluff, real results

ux_norms: active workout mode is full screen — zero distractions, only workout controls visible
all tap targets during active workout minimum 56px — hands are sweaty, precision is low
timer is always the most prominent element during workouts — largest text on screen
quick start — maximum 2 taps from home to first set logged
rest timer starts automatically after set logged — user can dismiss or extend, never ignore
personal records (PRs) always celebrated — animation on PR beaten, badge on summary
workout tracker screens: home shows today's planned workout if program active — never generic feed
workout tracker screens: active workout input for weight and reps always uses large number keypad — never small text input
workout tracker screens: previous performance shown above each exercise input row — instant comparison without navigating away
workout tracker screens: workout summary always shows total volume, duration, muscles worked, and PRs beaten
workout tracker screens: exercise library filters by muscle group first — most common lookup pattern
workout tracker screens: progress screen leads with strength charts — body weight is secondary unless goal is weight loss
wearable integration expected at startup and scale — heart rate zone visible during active workout when connected
streaks and achievements drive daily engagement — streak count always visible on home screen

visual_language.style: high energy action photography — powerful, aspirational, diverse
photography_rules: action shots preferred over static poses
diverse body types and ages — fitness is for everyone
never use overly airbrushed or unrealistic imagery
visual_language.background_treatment: dark and powerful OR high contrast light — never pastel or soft
visual_language.empty_state_style: bold SVG — dumbbell, fire, or trophy with motivating copy
visual_language.onboarding_visual: bold flat vector or energetic photography — powerful theme
visual_language.illustration_style: when used: bold geometric vector — strong shapes, high contrast

compliance_notes: medical disclaimer required for fitness advice
injury risk warnings on high intensity content
data handling for health metrics (HIPAA adjacent)
age restrictions for certain training programmes
GDPR for biometric and health data

avoid: Never show weight or body composition data in a context that could trigger body image concerns
Never use before/after imagery without informed consent framing
Never gamify injury recovery — medical guidance supersedes engagement mechanics
Never fabricate performance benchmarks or calorie burn estimates as precise facts
Never use aggressive or shaming language in notifications or empty states
Never make rest days feel like failures — rest is training
enforce: Exercise instructions always include form cues and injury prevention notes
Rest day suggestions always framed positively — recovery is progress
Heart rate zones shown with health context — not just numbers
Medical disclaimer on any content that could affect health decisions
User's own PBs and progress always the primary benchmark — not others'
Emergency stop option always visible during any guided workout
